title: StratusMarket & Redwood: Joint Marketplace Listing + Reference Architecture Workshop
next_steps: Redwood to draft reference architecture doc (initial version) and share by 2025-04-15
StratusMarket to provide marketplace listing template and seller account contact by 2025-04-10
SEs to run VPC connectivity smoke test (private deployment path) and share logs
Schedule follow-up technical workshop focused on entitlements & metering (w/in 2 weeks)
action_items: Maya Chen: produce draft ref-arch diagram + deployment matrix by 2025-04-15
Diego Alvarez: create test checklist for VPC peering and KMS integration by 2025-04-11
Priya Nair: supply StratusMarket marketplace seller onboarding doc and contact by 2025-04-10
Rajesh Patel: confirm expected usage metering fields and sample manifests by 2025-04-13
summary: Working session to align on requirements for listing Redwood-backed inference offerings on StratusMarket's SaaS and AMI marketplaces, and to define a joint reference architecture for customers choosing hosted, dedicated, and private deployment patterns. Key outcomes: agreement on owner roles, deliverables and an initial plan to validate VPC private connectivity and entitlement/metering flows.
topics: Marketplace listing artifacts (SaaS listing vs AMI vs container)
Reference architecture components (VPC peering, SAML, KMS, audit logs)
Packaging options (BYOL, SaaS, dedicated pool images)
Entitlement and metering integration for billing
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. We'll go through the listing requirements and then the proposed ref arch. Diego and Renee are with me from infra, Omar's on solutions.
[00:00:12] Priya Nair: Thanks Maya. From StratusMarket we'll have Liam who is our solutions architect and Rajesh ops, and I'll own the marketplace onboarding.
[00:00:23] Liam O'Connor: Hi all. Quick note, we have a 60 minute slot, we'll try to keep Q&A to the end but interrupt if we need to.
[00:00:30] Diego Alvarez: Cool. I'll share my screen in a sec — bear with occasional screen flinch, my VPN's being moody today.
[00:00:40] Sara Kim: No worries. We just want to make sure timelines are realistic.
[00:00:44] Maya Chen: Agenda: 1) Listing types and artifact needs, 2) Ref-arch for Hosted/Dedicated/Private paths, 3) Entitlement and metering, 4) Security & compliance sync, 5) Next steps.
[00:00:58] Priya Nair: Sounds great. We especially want the details around private deployments and how entitlements work for reserved capacity.
[00:01:08] Diego Alvarez: Right. Quick framing: Redwood exposes the same API across modes — hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, and private deployments. For marketplace we usually offer a SaaS listing for hosted, a marketplace AMI/container for dedicated, and a private package (VPC-friendly install) for private customers.
[00:01:24] Liam O'Connor: When you say "private package", are we talking a full AMI with installer or a terraform module + chart?
[00:01:31] Diego Alvarez: Ideally both. For private customers we'd provide a helm chart + terraform infra module; for quick start we can also provide a pre-baked AMI or container image with the runtime and an installer script. The chart will reference KMS/HSM integrations and optional private key material handling.
[00:01:47] Rajesh Patel: For StratusMarket marketplace, our ops folks want a clear list of deliverables per listing type: what manifests, what installer scripts, expected IAM roles, networking requirements — those sort of things.
[00:01:58] Maya Chen: We'll create a table mapping listing type -> artifacts. E.g., SaaS: OpenAPI spec, branding assets, SSO metadata, SLA terms, onboarding runbook. AMI/container listing: image manifest, SBOM, EULA, terraform/helm quickstart, security checklist. Private package: helm/chart, terraform module, offline install bundle, KMS integration guide.
[00:02:18] Sara Kim: A couple of add-ons: audit logging format (CloudTrail vs custom), and whether customers expect native single-tenant VLANs.
[00:02:26] Diego Alvarez: Noted. Also worth flagging: our Dedicated offering supports reserved GPU pools behind autoscaling; the marketplace AMI for dedicated should include a small agent that signals usage back to entitlement/metering.
[00:02:40] Liam O'Connor: How do you handle metering for reserved capacity? If someone buys a monthly commit via marketplace, how does the marketplace get the usage info to reconcile billing?
[00:02:49] Omar Idris: Good question. We have two models: push and pull. For SaaS we push usage events to a metering API or we can provide periodic usage reports. For marketplace consumption, we can integrate with the marketplace metering service (if they expose one). For reserved capacity, we usually sync allocations using an entitlement API — the marketplace grants entitlement IDs which map to customer pools.
[00:03:07] Priya Nair: StratusMarket supports both an entitlement token exchange and a metering callback. We'll share the API spec.
[00:03:13] Maya Chen: Perfect. Diego will take point on implementing the lightweight agent for AMI/container so it knows how to emit the proper metering fields.
[00:03:21] Diego Alvarez: Yep. That agent will report token counts, inference latency percentiles, and GPU hours. We probably should also emit model version to avoid reconciliation drift when customers upgrade.
[00:03:33] Priya Nair: Regarding model versions, Stratus requires an explicit model version column in the metering payload. Good to know.
[00:03:38] Liam O'Connor: Switching gears to networking: for private deployments we need to validate VPC connectivity patterns. Stratus supports marketplace private offers where the SaaS vendor deploys into customer VPC via a private link or peering, or the customer deploys vendor images. Which patterns do you prefer?
[00:03:53] Diego Alvarez: We support three patterns: 1) customer-deployed private package (they install into their VPC), 2) vendor-deployed into customer VPC via controlled account (we have a private control plane option), 3) hybrid where the inference runtime sits in the vendor infra but uses private connectivity for uploads/telemetry. For compliance-heavy customers, customer-deployed (pattern 1) is most common.
[00:04:12] Sara Kim: Does customer-deployed require KMS key rotation guidance? Our customers ask about key lifecycle a lot.
[00:04:17] Diego Alvarez: Yes — the chart has hooks for KMS integration. We also support bringing-your-own-KMS, with HSM options for on-prem. We'll include a KMS integration guide in the private package artifacts.
[00:04:27] Liam O'Connor: Ok. On SSO and provisioning — Stratus uses SAML for the console and OIDC for API token exchange in some cases. Can you accept both?
[00:04:36] Maya Chen: Yes. Redwood Console supports SAML SSO for UI and OIDC for service tokens. We'll provide sample IdP metadata for the SaaS listing and an RBAC mapping guide for dedicated/private deployments.
[00:04:46] Priya Nair: Great. Now, security questionnaire items — we have a standard vendor questionnaire. How should we manage that?
[00:04:54] Reneé Park: We can fill the questionnaire but prefer to attach our SOC2 and ISO docs. We should also provide a summary of network controls and encryption at rest/in transit. There may be some items flagged where we need to get engineering signoff.
[00:05:06] Rajesh Patel: If possible, include a short runbook for incident response and contact points. Ops teams appreciate that when validating listings.
[00:05:12] Diego Alvarez: We'll include an incident response overview and sample contact matrix.
[00:05:17] Liam O'Connor: On the ref-arch: do you have a diagram we can iterate on?
[00:05:21] Diego Alvarez: Yes I'll share. [screen share noise], sorry if my cursor's not precise.
[00:05:30] [00:05:30] Diego Alvarez: (screen) Top left: Hosted SaaS path — requests hit Redwood API Gateway, routed to inference cluster, caches for KV cache prefixing, then model runtime. Top right: Dedicated — marketplace customer gets reserved pool; a broker handles routing and autoscaling. Bottom: Private — terraform + helm install inside customer VPC, optional private control plane for management.
[00:05:53] Priya Nair: Could you clarify the "broker" term? In marketplace context we'd like to see a black box integration point for entitlement checks.
[00:06:01] Omar Idris: Broker is our internal name for the component that does routing and entitlement validation. For marketplace integration, it can validate tokens against Stratus entitlements, and fallback to compatible model variants if capacity constrained.
[00:06:15] Liam O'Connor: Fallback behavior is important. If the customer restricts to a specific instance type because of compliance, do you support policy-based routing?
[00:06:23] Diego Alvarez: Yes, policy-based routing is supported. We can map entitlements to model variants or cheaper quantized models when latency targets are relaxed. We'll document routing policy examples in the ref-arch.
[00:06:33] Priya Nair: For marketplace listing pages, our UX team expects a short description, pricing model, and sample performance numbers. Can you provide a performance profile per model (latency p50/p95 at 128 tokens, cost per 1k tokens)?
[00:06:47] Maya Chen: We have verified performance profiles. We'll provide a one-page benchmark summary for each model variant targeted at the marketplace. Note: these are workload dependent and include caveats about sequence length and batching.
[00:06:58] Rajesh Patel: On billing — Stratus allows both recurring subscription (commit) and consumption billing. For commit we need an obvious mapping to reserved pool IDs so we can unlock features in the console.
[00:07:07] Diego Alvarez: We'll emit entitlements with reserved_pool_id and usage tokens for metering. The agent for AMI will include the reserved_pool_id in its heartbeat.
[00:07:14] Liam O'Connor: How will upgrades be handled for AMIs? If you ship an AMI and then there's a patch, do customers re-launch or do you provide patch channels?
[00:07:23] Diego Alvarez: For AMIs we provide versioned images and a small agent that can apply hot patches or schedule maintenance windows. We'll include a patching policy in the listing contract.
[00:07:33] Sara Kim: Can you support offline installs for air-gapped customers?
[00:07:37] Diego Alvarez: Yes, the private package can be exported as an offline bundle with a signed installer and SBOM. That is very common for regulated industries.
[00:07:44] Priya Nair: Perfect. Now a couple of nitty-gritty marketplace fields: pricing metadata, SKU ids, entitlements mapping, and fake-usage demos for the listing page.
[00:07:55] Maya Chen: We'll prepare a pricing metadata template. For demos, we can provide a sandbox listing with throttled quotas so Stratus can show sample usage without incurring production costs.
[00:08:06] Liam O'Connor: Co-marketing — Stratus likes a joint solution brief and a co-branded reference architecture. Do you have assets?
[00:08:12] Renee Park: Yes, marketing can supply a 1-pager, a AF doc of capabilities, and logo pack. We'll align on co-marketing collateral once the technical bits are ironed out.
[00:08:21] Priya Nair: Good. On technical validation, we want to do two pilots: 1) Marketplace SaaS listing validation using a test account, 2) Private package install into one of our enterprise lab VPCs. Can you support that?
[00:08:34] Omar Idris: Absolutely. We'll need credentials and a small lab env from Stratus for the VPC deploy. Diego will run the install and capture logs; Maya will coordinate the marketplace sandbox.
[00:08:44] Rajesh Patel: We'll spin up a lab VPC and share connection details. Expect network whitelists and temporary keys.
[00:08:50] Liam O'Connor: Timing — what's realistic for the initial pilot?
[00:08:54] Maya Chen: If we get the seller onboarding info by Friday, in two weeks we can get a sandbox demo and a basic private install validation — so target 2025-04-22 for first pilot artifacts.
[00:09:07] Priya Nair: That aligns with our PM timeline.
[00:09:10] [00:09:10] Diego Alvarez: Quick deep-dive on the agent for AMI/container: it will be lightweight Go binary, TLS mutual auth with our broker, expose a local prometheus endpoint for metrics, and send aggregated metering events every 5 minutes.
[00:09:26] Liam O'Connor: Mutual TLS — that implies we need cert exchange steps documented.
[00:09:30] Diego Alvarez: Yep we'll include CSR flow and CA pinning example in the private package.
[00:09:35] Sara Kim: In the security questionnaire, there are some questions around data retention and deletion. How do you surface deletion APIs for telemetry?
[00:09:42] Diego Alvarez: We support data retention policies per-tenant. Telemetry logs can be set to be purged on a schedule, and we expose a deletion API for customer data when requested under contract.
[00:09:52] Priya Nair: For SOC2/ISO proof, do you have an attestation we can attach to listing?
[00:09:57] Reneé Park: Yes, we'll provide SOC2 Type II report redacted as needed, and ISO summary.
[00:10:03] Liam O'Connor: Ok. Switching to the ref-arch doc sections — we'll need a networking diagram, components list, sequence diagram for entitlement exchange, and manifest examples.
[00:10:12] Diego Alvarez: We'll produce a doc with those sections. For sequence: 1) Customer purchases on Stratus marketplace -> 2) Marketplace issues entitlement -> 3) Customer retrieves entitlement (if customer-deployed) or marketplace sends to Redwood (vendor-deployed) -> 4) Redwood broker validates and unlocks pool or schedules provisioning.
[00:10:31] Priya Nair: That sequence is ideal. Also include failure modes — e.g., entitlement not found, capacity exceeded, fallback to public model.
[00:10:40] Omar Idris: Good point. We'll include automated fallback policies and notification hooks for ops.
[00:10:45] [00:10:45] Liam O'Connor: A few questions from our engineering team: 1) Are there size limits for images? 2) Do you publish SBOMs? 3) What's your expected footprint for an on-prem install?
[00:10:56] Diego Alvarez: 1) We prefer images <50GB for AMIs but can support larger if necessary; compressed container images are usually under 8GB. 2) Yes, SBOMs will be provided. 3) On-prem footprint depends on model family — a small footprint for quantized models (8-16GB GPU + 32GB RAM); large models require bigger nodes. We'll include a sizing table.
[00:11:19] Priya Nair: Can you also provide terraform examples that wire up KMS, subnets, and security groups?
[00:11:24] Diego Alvarez: Yes that's part of the terraform module. We'll include examples for AWS and Azure.
[00:11:29] Liam O'Connor: About Azure marketplace — Stratus has both Azure and AWS marketplaces. Are there any Azure-specific docs needed?
[00:11:36] Maya Chen: Azure has its own images and private offers mechanics. We'll produce an Azure-specific companion doc that maps to Stratus's seller flow. Diego will coordinate with an Azure infra SME if needed.
[00:11:47] Priya Nair: We'll share the seller account contacts for both clouds.
[00:11:51] Sara Kim: Are you planning to publish reference workloads (e.g., a sample chat app) for the marketplace listing?
[00:11:58] Renee Park: Yes. We can provide a small reference app and a walkthrough notebook that demonstrates common use cases: chat, summarization, embeddings. That helps buyers evaluate quickly.
[00:12:08] Liam O'Connor: On support SLAs — Stratus listings often show an expected support tier. How does Redwood map support tiers to marketplace SKUs?
[00:12:16] Maya Chen: We can map support tiers as add-on SKUs or as part of the subscription. We'll present options in the pricing metadata.
[00:12:25] Priya Nair: One more compliance note: our finance team needs to know if there are export controls on model binaries.
[00:12:31] Omar Idris: We'll include an export control checklist and label models that have restrictions.
[00:12:36] Ryan? [unintelligible]
[00:12:38] Speaker 1: (murmur)
[00:12:40] Priya Nair: Sorry, ignore that. Back to pilots: once we do the private install test we should capture a short runbook and a video. Can you produce a 10–15 minute install video?
[00:12:50] Diego Alvarez: Yes we'll make a condensed installer video and a step-by-step runbook.
[00:12:55] Liam O'Connor: Regarding telemetry — what PII, if any, is included in your logs?
[00:13:01] Diego Alvarez: Minimal. We try to avoid PII in telemetry; request IDs and hash pointers are used. Customer data is encrypted in transit and at rest. We'll add a data classification table in the security docs.
[00:13:11] Priya Nair: Great. A couple of lower level items: can you sign the Stratus standard marketplace indemnity clause?
[00:13:17] Renee Park: We'll review legal terms and coordinate with Redwood legal — we'll aim for a quick turnaround but may need negotiation on some clauses.
[00:13:25] Rajesh Patel: Ok team, what's left for our side — we'll prepare the sandbox and seller onboarding materials and share by Friday.
[00:13:32] Maya Chen: That's great. To recap the owners: Maya leads ref-arch doc; Diego leads agent/terraform/helm artifacts; Reneé handles security & legal; Priya owns seller onboarding from Stratus side; Rajesh will provide ops lab for VPC testing.
[00:13:46] Priya Nair: I'll also connect you with our product UX for the listing page to ensure the fields line up.
[00:13:52] Liam O'Connor: Can we get a short checklist now?
[00:13:56] Maya Chen: Sure: 1) Redwood to share draft ref-arch by 2025-04-15, 2) Stratus to share seller template and dev lab by 2025-04-10, 3) Diego will produce agent code sample and test checklist by 2025-04-11, 4) schedule follow-up workshop in 7–10 days.
[00:14:12] Priya Nair: Sounds good. A question from my ops person — what telemetry endpoints will you need opened?
[00:14:18] Diego Alvarez: We'll request outbound TLS to our broker on port 443 and a couple of specific IP ranges for control plane. We'll provide those IPs to Rajesh in a separate doc.
[00:14:27] Liam O'Connor: Anything on pricing sensitivity? Some of our larger customers push back on per-token pricing.
[00:14:33] Maya Chen: We offer both per-token and committed monthly pricing. For marketplace, we can present both as options or tier them as SKUs. We'll include an example compare table.
[00:14:42] Priya Nair: Ok. Last block — legal/contracting timeline. We typically want to have T&Cs sorted before listing — is 3 weeks realistic for Redwood?
[00:14:51] Reneé Park: Possibly. We'll fast-track initial T&Cs; some items may need legal review but we'll aim for 3 weeks.
[00:14:58] Liam O'Connor: Great. Anything else?
[00:15:00] Rajesh Patel: We'll get the lab VPC details by tomorrow EOD.
[00:15:03] Maya Chen: Fantastic. We'll follow up with the artifact checklist and kickoff a shared drive for artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[00:15:10] Priya Nair: Thanks all. Looking forward to the drafts.
[00:15:13] Liam O'Connor: Bye.

[Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-heard words and filler; speaker attributions approximate. The team agreed on deliverables and pilots. Expected dates and owners are in action items.]
